title: DUCX: Decomposing Unfairness in Tool-Using Chest X-ray Agents

bias_targets.methodology: The paper evaluates disparities between male and female patients in chest X-ray agents by decomposing unfairness into tool exposure bias (accuracy gaps conditioned on tool use), tool transition bias (differences in tool routing patterns), and LLM reasoning bias (differences in text generation quality and hedging), alongside standard end-to-end fairness metrics like Equalized Odds and Demographic Parity.

The paper evaluates disparities between younger (<60) and older (≥60) patients in chest X-ray agents by decomposing unfairness into tool exposure bias (accuracy gaps conditioned on tool use), tool transition bias (differences in tool routing patterns), and LLM reasoning bias (differences in text generation quality and hedging), alongside standard end-to-end fairness metrics like Equalized Odds and Demographic Parity.
